confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'that pattern points strongly to the battery' and 'the lithium-ion cells in the original battery are probably worn out' without a swap test; also asserted the battery is original, which the customer did not know

rationale: The assistant correctly leaned towards a worn battery and used the Max-mode and light-pattern evidence, but it misidentified SV11 as a V10 (it is a V7) and described the 'original battery' as fact. It never asked whether the stop was a clean one or pulsing, never mentioned checking the charger or contacts, and never suggested Dyson support for diagnosis. It advised against the battery and towards replacing the whole vacuum, a conclusion built on the wrong model and unsupported cost reasoning, so the customer's actual question about a roughly £60 battery was answered poorly. It also earlier gave a wrong hint that the model code sat on the motor bar.
